intro: Squamish has local buses, but no public bus to Vancouver or Whistler. Private coach companies have run the route. A public service along Highway 99 was first proposed in the 2015 Sea to Sky Transit Future Plan and studied again in 2017.

The 2017 study's first phase called for eight buses and six weekday round trips between Vancouver and Whistler, costing about $3.3 million a year. Local governments together would have paid about $1.9 million and the Province about $1.4 million. Those are 2017 estimates and would be higher today.

The idea has stalled over who runs it and who pays. A regional transit commission and a small local fuel tax were proposed but have not moved forward. In September 2026 the Sea to Sky Regional Transit Committee, which includes the District of Squamish, signed a memorandum with the Province to keep planning governance, funding and service. No cost share for Squamish has been set as of October 2026.

timeline.what: BC Transit's Sea to Sky Transit Future Plan first proposed a bus between corridor communities.
The Regional Transit Study set out options and led to the Sea to Sky Regional Transit Committee.
The committee and the Province signed a memorandum to plan governance, funding and a service model together.

sides.answer: Yes, even with a small tax increase
points: Local money shows the Province that corridor communities are serious, and the bus can't start until local partners commit their share.
It gives people without a car, and commuters, a cheaper option than private coaches.
Highway 99 is a provincial road, and Squamish taxpayers already face big increases for local needs.
A provincial service could be built on a corridor wide funding model instead of town by town budgets.
Private coach companies already run the route, and town money is better spent on local buses and basics.
The yearly cost would be permanent and would likely grow.

questions.a: No share has been set. In 2017 the estimate for all local governments together was about $1.9 million a year.
The Lil'wat Nation, Village of Pemberton, Squamish Lillooet Regional District, Resort Municipality of Whistler, District of Squamish and the Squamish Nation, working with the Province.
No date has been set. The current memorandum is for planning only.
